page: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro Hypervisor, engineered for compute-heavy graphics, machine learning inference, and large-scale parallel processing. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running on x86_64 architecture with 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.4 GHz. It features a 320 MB L3 cache, hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and AVX-512 vector instructions. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 1024.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, yielding approximately 10.67 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by 4 NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, offering a combined 384 GB of GPU VRAM. Storage capabilities include 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, minimizing disk I/O bottlenecks for data-intensive applications. Networking throughput is defined by an 800 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating massive node-to-node data transfers and distributed dataset staging. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations show top-tier computational and memory performance. The system achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 21470.0, a PassMark CPU score of 91429.15, and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 85028.43. Its memory subsystem demonstrates high transfer rates, measuring 224.52 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 96.38 GB/sec on large-block writes. Ray tracing and image processing tasks benchmark in the top 10% bracket, recording scores of 95118.0 and 21579.0 respectively. While single-core stress-ng results are average at 2106.88, parallelized operations like bzip3 decompression reach 564.58 GB/sec.

For machine learning deployment, the quad-GPU configuration excels across large language model inference workloads. In prompt processing benchmarks, the instance yields 11391.36 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models, 7144.93 tokens/sec on 7B models, and 1278.65 tokens/sec on 70B parameter models. Text generation throughput tracks at 337.11 tokens/sec for 135M, 174.0 tokens/sec for 7B, and 28.21 tokens/sec for 70B models, placing the platform in the top tier across all model scales.

Given the density of 4 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, 1 TB of DDR5 memory, 7.6 TB of local NVMe storage, and 800 Gbps network bandwidth, the g7e.24xlarge offers high computational consolidation. Workloads that align with this profile include multi-GPU AI/LLM inference, 3D visualization, ray tracing pipelines, distributed data processing, and large in-memory databases.
description: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance designed for large-scale GPU computing, AI inference, and intensive data processing. Built on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 48 physical cores, 96 dedicated vCPUs, and 1024.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory. The hardware configuration includes 4 NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs delivering a total of 384 GB VRAM, bundled with 7600 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and an 800 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional throughput across parallel tasks, with top-tier rankings in ray tracing, image processing, multi-threaded decompression, and LLM prompt processing. Delivering high compute density per instance, the g7e.24xlarge is suited for 70B parameter LLM inference, 3D graphics rendering, computer vision, and large-scale real-time analytics pipelines.
